liam: note alternating kernel picks: some go `fp32_cpu` (slow) then fallback to `fallback_gpu` on retries. looks like the selector is misclassifying very short token sequences and under-batching them.

sam: that's probably the recent tweak to `kernel_selector.v2` that favors low-latency CPU path for <16 tokens. we rolled that 3h ago. @jess can you check rollout tags?

ana: also seeing KV cache churn in the same window. short requests displace entries so later longer requests miss and hit slower paths. sequence:
1) microburst short requests -> small batches -> fp32_cpu
2) repeated misses -> kv evictions
3) later requests trigger full recompute / kernel fallback

sam: looks like batching_heuristic underestimates throughput for high-QPS tiny-token workloads. continuous-batcher sends tiny batches too frequently which prevents GPU amortization.

jess: quick mitigation ideas:

- tune continuous_batcher minimum batch delay to 6ms
- sticky-kv policy: avoid evicting on tiny request footprints

ana: we can also short-circuit tool-call retries at the router to avoid oscillation between cpu/gpu kernels.
